claims.statement: The chat wire is still CopilotKit: the drop-CopilotKit plan's M3/M4 are not started (CHANGELOG), package.json still depends on @copilotkit/react-core and @copilotkit/runtime (~1.75.2) alongside @ag-ui/client 0.0.59, AgentProviders still mounts CopilotKitProvider at /api/copilotkit, and app/api/copilotkit/[[...slug]]/route.ts still exists.

Server components call the backend over REST via apiGet in lib/api/client.ts, whose base is AGENT_URL with the trailing /agent stripped, falling back to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL then http://localhost:8010; it attaches the caller's bearer token from serverAuthHeaders (the Supabase session access token, or Bearer dev:<email> from the sangam-dev-as cookie in dev-login mode) and throws NotFoundError on 404.

Chat does not call the backend from the browser: AgentProviders points CopilotKitProvider at /api/copilotkit, whose CopilotRuntime registers three HttpAgents (sangam_agent at AGENT_URL, sangam_ingest at AGENT_URL with /agent replaced by /ingest, sangam_proposal with /proposal) behind one createCopilotRuntimeHandler at basePath /api/copilotkit (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE) with an InMemoryAgentRunner and maxDuration 1800 to match the backend.

AGENT_URL must end in /agent (used verbatim for Ask, suffix swapped for Import, stripped for REST) while NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL has no suffix and is the browser-side REST base; docker compose sets AGENT_URL to the internal backend:8000/agent and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL to localhost:8010.

Client components do REST with fetch to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL using authHeaders() (Supabase session token, or Bearer dev:<email> in dev-login mode), with a shared call() helper in lib/api/rest.ts (moved from the now-removed features/ask/lib/rest.ts) that throws ApiError carrying status and body so callers can read a 409's detail; the same module exports API and getMe, and Funder Match, RFP Watch, Media, proposals, Import approval and the Registry's paged fetch use it.

proxy.ts runs Supabase updateSession on all non-static paths, refreshing the session via getClaims and redirecting signed-out visitors on /import (the only protected prefix) to /auth/login?next=; /ask stays public, and without Supabase env keys nothing is gated.

AgentProviders holds the access token (initial Supabase session plus onAuthStateChange, or the dev token in dev-login mode) and sends it as an Authorization Bearer header on chat requests; the auth callback only honours same-origin next paths via safeNextPath.

apiGet caches signed-out reads with next revalidate 300 only in production and only when there is no Authorization header, sending an x-sangam-build header (deployment id or commit SHA) so each deploy gets a fresh cache key; signed-in and development requests use no-store.

/ask is force-dynamic and checks the session server-side (getClaims, the dev cookie in dev-login mode, or signed-out if Supabase keys are missing): signed out it renders AskPreview (sample content, no agent call, question parked in sessionStorage across sign-in and prefilled but not sent); signed in it fetches an index payload plus /api/me via apiGet and renders the workspace with canScout; ?view=import redirects to /import.

The Ask workspace lazy-loads via next/dynamic so the CopilotKit runtime downloads only when rendered; AskWorkspace derives its screen from the address (?view= via viewFrom over WORKSPACE_VIEWS ask, chats, funder-match, proposals, rfpwatch, vault, media, declared in lib/workspaceUrl.ts and re-exported by Sidebar.tsx; ?proposal= and ?funder= as positive-integer ids; the chat from ?thread=), renders each view as a plain conditional, keys ChatPane by threadId so switching chats remounts it, and gives RfpWatchView onAsk (a new chat seeded with a question) and onFunderMatch callbacks.

Ask thread lists come from GET /api/threads with localStorage (sangam_threads_v1) only as a title fallback and for a just-started chat; reopened chats load saved messages from /api/threads/{id}/messages, where a 404 means an empty chat.

useAgentChat(threadId, runtimeAgentId, prefix, loadHistory) is the shared chat hook for Ask (sangam_agent), Scout (sangam_ingest) and the proposal chat (sangam_proposal): it wraps CopilotKit useAgent and folds messages into turns, turning tool calls into trace steps matched to tool results, excluding subagent-run prose from the answer, tracking subagent lane owners from live events only, loading history only after the agent is ready and empty, and running/stopping via copilotkit.runAgent/stopAgent.

The /import route is force-dynamic and redirects anyone who is not staff or a steward (canUseScout), or whose /api/me call fails, to /ask; it does not read ?thread= itself. ImportLoader lazy-loads ImportPage with ssr false; ImportShell takes the open thread from useUrlThread validated by isImportId (import-uuid), mirrors a draft's first send into the address with a replace, pushes ?thread= when a past run is picked, and lists past runs; ImportView loads all panels with a single GET /api/ingest/overview, offers no tasks until that answers (NO_ACCESS), derives ImportAccess {staff, stewardOf, orgs} from it, and shows team tools only to staff. In lib/access.ts tasksFor gives staff four tasks (funder, ngo, news, calls), stewards funder and ngo, and everyone else none; this only shapes the screen and the backend checks again.

Import pause cards (SourcesCard, SaveQuestions, ImportApproval) answer backend interrupts through CopilotKit useInterrupt with renderInChat false, rendered once into a single DOM node that ScoutChat portals into the visible layout; SaveQuestions resolves with the decision and slug so parallel paused writers can be addressed.

useRunPause records the tool a run stopped on from the interrupt custom event or a RunFinished with outcome interrupt, and ScoutChat disables its composer as stuck when the run is idle, no card is open and a pause is recorded.

Sources ticked before the first message are sent to the backend as AG-UI agent context with the exact description 'Sources the person ticked for this Import run', which the backend's TickedSources middleware looks up.

While an Import run is going, composer messages are not sent to the agent: askLive posts to /api/ingest/threads/{id}/ask-live and the backend answers from run state; text classified as an instruction is queued and sent as the next message after the run ends with no card open.

The Scout step shown in the UI (Start, Working, Review, Done) is derived on the client from isRunning, whether a review card is open and counts from DoneReport, with the working board built from the turn's tool steps and lane owners.

The drop-CopilotKit plan targets an out-of-memory failure in the relay (InMemoryAgentRunner buffering every event plus raw LangGraph event copies); its M3 would replace CopilotKit hooks with an @ag-ui/client HttpAgent talking directly to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL /agent and /ingest, delete the proxy route, and accept losing mid-run reload replay.

The design system lives in the Claude Design project 'Sangam Design System v2' (built 8 Oct 2026) as system of record; docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md still says there is no automatic sync, so it is synced by hand: the repo never invents a token the design system lacks, UI PRs that change frontend/components or UI-kit screens must update it in the same PR, tokens map one to one by CSS variable name to globals.css (with @theme inline re-exposing them to Tailwind), components are translated rather than copied, and rules fix corner radii, type scale, AA contrast, Lucide icons and a single page-max column.

Frontend code is organised as routes-only app/ (everything else goes in features/), one features/ folder per screen, components/ui and components/layout, and lib/; list pages share the BucketCards/FilterRow/SearchBox/ListMore pattern in components/ui/ListPage.tsx, with useShowMore for client-side paging (proposals list), useCursorList for server cursor paging (Media & Signals) and usePagedList for server limit/offset paging (Registry), and new list pages must reuse the pattern.

Proposals are server-backed: views/proposals/api.ts keeps a module-level cache of rows from GET /api/proposals behind useSyncExternalStore, reloads it after every mutation (start, save work, rename, delete, advance, save version), and the only browser storage left is a read of the legacy sangam.proposals.v1 key to show a notice that old browser-only proposals are not migrated; store.ts and start.ts no longer exist.

A proposal is started from a Funder Match card by naming it and POSTing /api/proposals with the org slug and funder id; the card only offers Start when the match list's may_run is true, so members can only view existing proposals.

ProposalShell renders five steps (Can you apply?, Your documents and style, Make a case, Make a plan, Before you send it) whose current number is owned by the server (work.stage); every edit is a PATCH /api/proposals/{id}/work with dotted keys, Continue calls POST advance and is disabled while summary.to_continue is non-empty (a 409 detail lists what is missing), and a stepper button is enabled only for an editor, for a step other than the current one and up to summary.furthest: an earlier step is a stage save, a later one POST advance?to=N.

Proposal editing is optimistic-concurrency aware and role-aware: PartEditor autosaves about 1.5 s after typing with the part's rev and on a 409 takes the other writer's text while keeping the person's own beneath it; can_edit from the server makes the screen read-only and hides the chat; the shell polls the proposal every 5 s while a file reader is running, or while an editor is at step 2+ and the chat has no send function yet, so teammates see progress.

The proposal chat (TellSangam, Sangam Pitch) uses useAgentChat against the sangam_proposal agent with the per-user proposal.thread_id (proposal-<id>-<user id>), loads history from /api/proposals/{id}/messages, sends the current step, selection and open part as AG-UI context under the exact description 'What the person is looking at', and answers proposal_question and proposal_suggestion interrupts through useInterrupt in QuestionCard.

Step 5's FinishCard smooths language through POST /api/proposals/{id}/polish (a 409 lists the differences when a figure, place, name or gap changed) and saves a Word version through POST /api/proposals/{id}/versions (with shape form to fill the funder's form), opening it through a short-lived /api/documents/{id}/file link; step 2's read-files and write-first-draft buttons, steps 3 and 4's Write <tab> and Write the Summary, and step 5's Rewrite are fixed messages sent to the proposal chat rather than REST calls, and are disabled while the chat cannot accept a message.

Local dev login: DEV_LOGIN in lib/devAuth.ts is true only when NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is unset and NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_AUTH=1; the navbar sign-in becomes a select of seeded @local.test users stored in the sangam-dev-as cookie, and /ask, serverAuthHeaders, authHeaders and AgentProviders use Bearer dev:<email> instead of a Supabase token.

Without the Supabase URL and publishable key (a bare local run) updateSession returns NextResponse.next and gates nothing, /ask's isSignedIn catches the failed client and shows the preview, and the sign-in dialog says the Supabase keys are not set and hides the Google button.

Registry profile pages (/registry/[slug] and /registry/funders/[slug]) are server components making one apiGet profile call, mapping NotFoundError to notFound() and permanently redirecting to the canonical slug; they render ProfileHero over client tab components (OrgProfileTabs, FunderProfileTabs) whose active tab is URL state via useUrlTab (?tab=, first tab is the bare URL) over the already-loaded profile, so a tab switch makes no request.

Legacy routes are bare redirects: /funders and /orgs go to /registry filtered by type, /methodology and /resources to /resources/methodology, /taxonomy to /resources/taxonomy keeping its anchor, and /privacy to /terms#t-collect.

The Ask sidebar is a collapsible workspace rail: expanded it offers New Chat, Recent Chats (first 5 threads, 'Show All' opens the chats view), Use Cases (Funder Match, Proposals, RFP Watch, Media & Signals) and Context (Doc Vault), with section open state held in the Sidebar so the icon-only collapsed rail (default on viewports up to 768px) can reopen it at a section; a Tools section linking to /import (Sangam Scout) appears only when canScout is true.

Unshipped Ask features are gated by one set, COMING_SOON in features/ask/lib/comingSoon.ts, which is now empty: a name in the set would show a 'Soon' tag in the sidebar and render ComingSoonView in place of the real view, and for 'proposals' would also hide the Funder Match proposal filter and disable MatchCard's Start a proposal button. With the set empty, Proposals and RFP Watch both render their real views (RfpWatchView is live). The signed-out AskPreview hard-codes its own 'RFP watch ... Coming soon' text and does not read the set, so it is out of date.

The home page (/) is a static server component, HomePage, with no backend call: hero with Ask Sangam and Explore the Registry buttons beside the cross-fading HeroSlides client component, a five-step agent explainer, source cards, partner logos and a Stay updated card whose Subscribe button has no submit handler.

The navbar (components/layout/Nav.tsx) exposes only Registry, Ask Sangam and Resources plus SignInButton, with a phone menu that closes when the pathname changes; /import is not linked from it (Scout is reached from the workspace sidebar), and NavBar highlights the section by first matching path prefix, mapping legacy /orgs, /funders, /methodology and /taxonomy to Registry or Resources and everything else to home.

The design system's token files map to globals.css by name: colors, typography and spacing to the :root variables, base.css to the hand-written classes (including the list-page classes and .toast), and five feature files imported in order after base.css: scout.css (Scout), registry.css (Registry list, profile, brief classes, .pill-tabs), registry-row.css (Registry row population chips, .reg-row-line, .reg-row-label, .reg-more and the filtered tag edge), site.css (Nav's .nav-links and phone menu, Home's .home-step*) and workspace.css last (Ask use-case screens: Funder Match .fm-*, RFP Watch .rfp-*, Sangam Pitch .pr-*, Media & Signals .story-*).

/registry is server-paged: the server page reads the filters from searchParams and makes one apiGet of GET /api/registry for the first 25 rows (PAGE) passed to RegistryClient as `first`, and the browser asks the server for later batches and for every filter or search change; RegistryClient no longer filters or pages in the browser. features/registry/rows.ts keeps only presentation (kindLine, signal, NORTH_EAST) and the filter rules live in the backend SQL. The Registrations filter shows only on the CSOs bucket and Funder type / How to approach only on Funders, and picking a bucket resets those. Filters are URL state (filtersFrom reads ?type=cso|funder and the other params, filterParams drops defaults, changes go through setUrlParams replace, registryQuery builds the API query from the same names).

A Registry row shows each theme domain its themes reach (backend order, Others last, an italic 'Themes not tagged yet' gap tag when none), SDG chips, an 'In <domain>:' line naming matching sub-themes when a Theme filter is set, and a 'Serves' line of up to three population tags with '+N more', moving a filtered population first and marking the filtered tag data-active.

ProfileHero draws a profile's tags as a facet list, using splitTags to separate themes (theme and sub_theme kinds), population tags (labelled by whoLabel) and lens tags, each on its own labelled line (Themes, who, Lenses, SDGs) with the ask and research-brief calls to action.

Home's five agent steps are a constant STEPS array rendered as one ol.home-steps card; pure CSS makes it a numbered vertical timeline below 900 px and five hairline-divided columns from 900 px up, with no step state.

Nav's phone menu: below 640 px the inline .nav-links hide and a 44 px menu button beside Sign in toggles a .nav-menu listing the same three links; Nav stores the pathname the menu was opened on (openOn) so it counts as open only on that pathname, and following a link also closes it; from 640 px up the button and menu are hidden by CSS.

Funder Match and RFP Watch both choose the organisation through useOrgChoices, which uses the page's /api/me result as a seed and calls getMe only without one (staff choose from every organisation, others from their memberships), and a signed-in person with no organisation sees an explanatory card instead of data; Funder Match keeps the chosen organisation in ?org= (replace, ignoring slugs that are not the person's choices) while RFP Watch keeps it in local state.

FunderMatchView reads the org's latest saved run from GET /api/funder-matches?org=, loads a card's detail from /api/funder-matches/{id}/detail only when 'Why this score' opens, and reruns via POST /api/funder-matches/runs (button shown only when the list's may_run is true, which also becomes mayStart on each card); strong and medium matches are ranked as cards with tier buckets, funder-type and proposal filters and search, while weak and not_scored rows are folded into a disclosure shown only at default filters.

RfpWatchView is the live RFP Watch screen: it loads GET /api/rfps/feed?org= and changes a call with PATCH /api/rfps/{id}/matches/{org_id} (flagged, saved, dismissed); the feed's can_act hides Save and 'Not for us' for people who cannot act; buckets are For you (open calls), Closing soon (within 30 days) and Saved (kept after the deadline), narrowed by search and theme; dismissed or unsaved closed calls are dropped locally; CallCard renders only http(s) links and 'Ask about this call' opens a new Ask chat with a prepared question.

In Scout, the news and calls tasks are pulls (isPull) that read no chosen sources, so no source picker is required before sending, while funder and NGO research blocks Send until sources are ticked; picking a task card only writes leadIn(task) into the composer, and the ScoutRail shows the picker before start and 'Reading from' afterwards.

ImportApproval picks one of three approval cards from the paused run_import_now sources argument: an open-calls card when sources contain funder_calls (adds calls to RFP Watch), a news card when they contain tavily_news (with a plan line from /api/ingest/news-runs/plan), otherwise the generic write-to-catalog card; all resolve with an approve or reject decision, and toolLabels labels a funder_calls run_import_now step as an open-calls import.

With Supabase keys missing, proxy.ts/updateSession passes every request through without redirecting, and the failure appears downstream as signed-out: /ask renders the preview, /import's server apiGet('/api/me') rejects and the page's catch turns it into a redirect to /ask, and the sign-in dialog says the keys are not set.

Registry rows and profiles surface funder approach: RegistryRow carries open_call and intake_mode, the row signal line can say 'open call now' and 'invites partners', the 'How to approach' filter is offered only when the server's approach facet reports an open call or invitation-only funder (and only on the Funders bucket), and the funder profile's Mandate tab lists open_calls from the single profile payload.

The Ask EvidenceRail builds its Sources list through sourcesFor in lib/sources.ts from three grains, de-duplicated by URL or label: fact rows parsed from the `sources:` block db_query appends to its result (a backend text contract), web entries from a fetch_url step's url argument, and entity entries for the org, funder, activity or score a citation marker points at, resolved from the IndexPayload; it shows at most MAX_SOURCES (10) with the remainder as a count and explains rows with no per-row source by naming the tables read.

Registry profile partner lists are paged after load: the profile payload carries only the first PartnerGroupPage, and usePartnerGroups fetches further pages from the browser with authHeaders() and next_cursor from /api/orgs/{slug}/funders (Funding tab) or /api/funders/{slug}/partners (Giving tab), appending groups and flagging an error if a page fails.

Screens live in the address using native history calls rather than router.push (because /ask is force-dynamic and a router navigation would refetch it): lib/url.ts provides withParams (null, undefined or empty drops a param), setUrlParams (push by default so Back undoes a screen change, replace for filters and fill-ins, no write when the address is unchanged), idParam and oneOf; useUrlTab reads ?tab= with the first tab as the bare URL. Ask's view, proposal and thread are pushes while Registry filters and Funder Match's org are replaces.

useUrlThread owns the open chat as ?thread=: a missing or invalid value (checked by the caller's valid function: isAskThreadId for Ask, isImportId for Import) is an unsent draft with a client-generated id; markSent names the draft in the address with a replace (no Back step); a sent draft that is left is replaced by a fresh one; resume is true when the id came from the address so saved messages load.

A sidebar pick in the Ask workspace writes viewParams(view): the chat is the bare URL and the previous screen's proposal, funder and org ids are cleared while ?thread= is kept; picking the screen already open does nothing except inside one proposal, which returns to the list; unknown ?view= values fall back to the chat.

Step 3 of a proposal carries a Secondary research card whose buttons call REST directly rather than the chat (POST /api/proposals/{id}/research to search, DELETE to delete or start fresh), because a search can outlast the chat stream; Research deeper first fetches editable angles from GET /research/angles and then sends them to the proposal chat, and only once parts A2 and A3 are marked done.

The proposal chat floats over the page in a panel opened by a Sangam Pitch button, shown only to editors; the panel is hidden rather than unmounted so a turn keeps streaming while it is closed, and the screen context sent to the agent includes the step, selected text and, on steps 3 and 4, the open part.

/settings is a server component that reads the Supabase user and /api/me, shows the account, memberships and an OrgMembersCard per administered organisation, and gives staff a StaffMembersCard to pick any organisation and manage its members through /api/orgs/{id}/members; unlike /ask it does not catch a failed Supabase client when the keys are missing.

The frontend has a Vitest suite (npm test): *.test.ts run in node for pure modules, *.test.tsx in jsdom with tests/setup.ts, which mocks next/navigation (a mutable search) and next/link; the URL-state contract (push versus replace, defaults out of the address, invalid ids ignored, round trips) is pinned by lib/__tests__/url-hooks.test.tsx and back-navigation.test.ts.

The CopilotKit proxy route serves only the routes the chat client calls: the handler's onBeforeHandler hook runs allowRoute, an allow-list of info, agent/run, agent/connect, agent/stop and agent/suggest; every other runtime route (threads/*, memories/*, inspector/*, transcribe, annotate, cpk-debug-events) throws a 404 Response, because the runtime's in-memory store would otherwise hand out other users' runs. Chat history comes from the backend's /api/threads instead, and a unit test pins both lists.

Doc Vault uploads never pass through the backend: uploadToVault POSTs /api/documents/uploads for a signed URL, PUTs the file straight to Supabase Storage, then POSTs /api/documents to record it (a Vercel Function body cap is below the size of large PDFs), mapping 503, 403 and 415 to specific messages. The same lib/vault.ts helpers are used by VaultView and by step 2 of the proposal shell.

VaultView shows a Delete button (behind a confirm dialog) only to staff and only for rows with doc_type vault_upload; AskWorkspace passes isStaff from payload.me, and deleteFromVault maps 403, 404 and 409 to friendly messages. The backend still enforces the staff-only rule.

The research-brief pages fetch a signed-URL BriefLink with apiGet, fetch the markdown fresh (no-store, throwing on failure) and render it via parseBrief, a line parser coupled to the backend's brief.py entity_markdown format: it strips HTML comments robustly, reads the special sections and findings, folds findings that quote the same sentence from the same source and year, and stops at a --- line.

Scout review rows (ReviewFields.tsx) label each finding Confirmed or Self-reported with a proof disclosure, render staff-workbook findings (made-up host staff-sources.sangam.invalid) as 'Your team's spreadsheet' and private findings as the person's own document (tagged not saved when held), and only link http(s) source URLs, re-checking them client-side.

usePagedList (components/ui/ListPage.tsx) is the offset twin of useCursorList: it is keyed by a resetKey so a filter change restarts at offset 0 and a stale answer is dropped, it uses an optional server-rendered `first` page for the opening key without refetching, skips duplicate ids, exposes `more` only while rows remain and no load is running, and reports `fetched` so ListMore's trigger is not stranded by a dropped duplicate.

The Registry's bucket counts and dropdown options come from the server and only on the first page: the backend returns counts and facets only when offset is 0, covering the whole Registry regardless of filters, and RegistryClient reads them from the server-rendered `first`, so they stay fixed while the person filters or scrolls; the 'Works in' options are the North-East states present in the where facet.

On the Registry, typed search text is held locally and copied to the address while the server is asked about it only after SEARCH_DELAY_MS (250 ms) of no typing; dropdown, bucket and Clear picks are asked at once; later batches go through fetchRegistryPage (call() in lib/api/rest.ts) from the browser, and search matches anywhere in the entity's name, aliases, districts, states, programme and partner names.

GET /api/registry returns a RegistryPage (FacetedPage<RegistryRow>: items, total, limit, offset, counts, facets) built by one SQL query that applies the filters and search and orders CSOs first then funders A→Z; research counts are added to the returned rows only, a failure there is logged and the page still returns, and each row's search text is excluded from the response. The frontend mirrors this in Page<T>, Facet, FacetedPage<T> and RegistryPage in lib/api/types.ts.
